subject: Sizing + SLA tradeoffs for high-concurrency conversational stack
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@curative.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask — live chat agent workload + pricing overview

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this. We put together an initial workload snapshot and a short set of goals for our dedicated deployment. High-level:
- Production chat assistants for customer support (multi-turn).
- Baseline traffic: ~60 requests/sec (steady daytime).
- Peak: sustained 200–240 requests/sec during incident windows (~1–2 hours).
- Concurrency: simultaneous active sessions ~160–220.
- Median input context: 900 tokens (users + chat history).
- Typical generation target: 80 tokens average.
- Desired P95 latency target: <= 200ms for generation (we understand this varies by model/context).
- Model: currently evaluating 30–70B decoder-only models; expect to quantize to 4-bit.

Can you recommend a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) sizing that balances cost vs. throughput guarantees? Also want to understand committed discounts for 12/24 month terms and what SLA/throughput guarantees come with those commits (and what trade-offs are available: burst capacity, fallback model variants, pre-warming). Attached a CSV with per-endpoint QPS samples and token histograms.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

—Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of ML Infrastructure, CurativeAI

Subject: RE: Sizing ask — internal draft recommendations

Team — I ran the CSV through our throughput estimator and sketched two defensible options. Notes and assumptions are inline.

Assumptions (derived from workload_report.csv + call notes):
- Effective tokens/request = input (900) + output (80) = 980 tokens average.
- Peak sustained requests/sec = 220 (we should design for 10% headroom -> 242 rps).
- Concurrency maps roughly 1 inference per active session during bursts.
- Model family: 40–70B; quantized 4-bit gives ~2.2–2.8x token throughput vs fp16 on the same hardware depending on kernels.

Option A — SLO-first (lower risk, higher cost)
- Hardware: 4x H100 (or equivalent H2 class).
- Expected sustained throughput (baseline): ~260 rps for 80-token generation @ 980 tokens total (after quantization and batching).
- Headroom for bursts: can absorb spikes to ~360 rps by short-lived autoscaling/burst capacity (adds ephemeral GPUs).
- Guarantees: 99.9% uptime SLA; throughput SLO: sustained 220 rps with P95 latency <= 220ms for configured model variant.
- Commit recommendation: 12-month reserved pool with optional burst credits.
- Cost signal: premium pricing; discount tier ~18% off on list for 12mo commit.

Option B — Cost-optimized (trade some tail latency for lower price)
- Hardware: 6x A100-class (quantized runtime tuned).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~240 rps (higher aggregate capacity but slightly worse tail latency under peak due to fewer headroom GPUs).
- Burst handling: rely on model fallback (smaller 13B variant) for extreme tails; legal/regulatory note: fallback requires approval if you need deterministic model variant.
- Guarantees: 99.5% uptime SLA; throughput SLO: sustained 200 rps with P95 latency <= 300ms.
- Commit recommendation: 12- or 24-month reserved commit; 24-month gets steeper discount (26% off list).

Other trade-offs / options
- Quantization profile: we can validate your eval set to confirm quality at 4-bit. If quality regresses on key prompts, we'll recommend mixed-precision for specific routes (adds cost).
- Autoscale policy: prefer a small reserved core (the pool above) + burst credits (hourly/ephemeral). Burst credits priced at marginal rate with guaranteed preemption order.
- Monitoring: include token-level spend dashboards and per-route latency budgets in Redwood Console.

Next steps: I can convert Option A/B to concrete GPU-hour pricing and show monthly committed dollar amounts + discount math. Also will produce expected tokens/sec and tokens/min numbers for both options.

—Marissa

Hi Aisha / Procurement — attaching a sketched commercial proposal based on Marissa's two options. Highlights below.

Commercial highlights:
- Option A (SLO-first): 4x H100 dedicated pool, 12-month reserved commit = $112,500/month list -> 18% discount = $92,250/month. Included: 2000 burst credits/month, 24/7 priority support, 99.9% uptime SLA, throughput SLO (sustained 220 rps).
- Option B (Cost-opt): 6x A100 equivalent pool, 12-month reserved commit = $86,000/month list -> 22% discount = $66,680/month. Included: 1200 burst credits/month, business-hours support, 99.5% uptime SLA, throughput SLO (sustained 200 rps).
- 24-month commit: additional 8% off the discounted rate (effectively ~26% total on Option B).
- Onboarding credit: one month of pool capacity credited for contracts signed within 30 days of this proposal.

SLA / guarantee notes:
- Our throughput SLOs are conditional on the model variant you pin. If you'd like deterministic behavior for specific endpoints, we can lock model image & kernel set in production.
- Burst capacity: ephemeral GPUs are subject to availability and a preemption window; guaranteed burst credits are only included with higher commit tiers.

Attachments: proposed_contract_v1.pdf (contains MSA + Exhibit A with commit math and sample rollback terms).

If the pricing looks reasonable, we can: 1) sign an LOI for the 12mo Option B (fast path) and schedule an onboarding deep-dive to surface any eval regressions, or 2) schedule a technical deep-dive to benchmark quantized runtimes against your key prompts.

—Ben Carter
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
